author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Ranger Suárez worked seven strong innings and the Boston Red Sox scored in each of their final three turns at bat to beat the Kansas City Royals 5-1 Saturday at Fenway Park. The victory stopped Boston’s three-game losing streak and moved the club to 81-68.

Suárez allowed one run on five hits, struck out eight and completed 96 pitches. Wilyer Abreu broke a 1-1 tie with a two-run double in the sixth after singles by Mickey Gasper and Adley Rutschman. Nick Sogard doubled and scored on Caleb Durbin’s single in the seventh, then Trevor Story and Sogard hit consecutive doubles for another run in the eighth.

Roman Anthony, Rutschman and Sogard each had multiple hits. Kansas City’s only run came on Carter Jensen’s 24th homer of the season, a solo shot inside Pesky’s Pole in the sixth. Garrett Whitlock struck out the side in a scoreless eighth and Aroldis Chapman finished the ninth without allowing a run.
dek: The left-hander allowed one run over seven innings as Boston ended a three-game skid at Fenway Park.
headline: Ranger Suárez carries Red Sox past Royals 5-1
